notes.decision: Obscure verb in physically-present text. Context (Father of Life + Mother of Living + Man up from the Deep + 'toward the mystery') suggests a verb of motion/passage. Possibly Greek-derived παράγω 'pass through, pass forth' adapted to Lycopolitan; or related to ⲡⲱⲣⲱ 'extend.' Tentatively rendered 'had passed forth.' Not in apparatus because the text is physically present.
ⲛ̄ here read as the verb 'bring' (Sahidic ⲉⲓⲛⲉ in its conjugated form ⲛ̄-) with First Man as object. The Living Spirit 'brings' the First Man up from the war — standard Manichaean cosmogonic action.
= ϩⲟⲉⲓⲙ 'wave.' The First Man is rescued from 'all the waves' of the war with Darkness — standard Manichaean cosmogonic image.
ⲍⲣⲁⲩ = ϩⲣⲟⲟⲩ 'voice' with 3pl suffix. 'Their voice came to him from on high' — the Lights of the upper realm address the ascending First Man with the words of Ps 110:1.
'My firstborn' — ϣⲁⲙⲓⲥⲉ = ϣⲁⲣⲡ̄ⲙⲓⲥⲉ per accumulated vocabulary. Here applied to the First Man as God's firstborn, addressed in the words of Ps 110:1.
Read as ϫⲉ-ⲉϥⲁ-ϣⲱⲡⲉ 'so that he might become' (purposive ϫⲉ + future). Fits the syntactical context of receiving ordination in order to become leader.
'The great gives authority to the small' (ⲧ = ϯ 'give'). The ecclesiastical correspondence to the First Man's enthronement: the rite of ordination as transmission of authority from greater to lesser.
= Sahidic ϭⲟⲙ 'power.' Lycopolitan ⲅ for ϭ. 'The powers of darkness' — standard Manichaean designation for the archonic forces in whose midst Mankind exists.

Read as ⲧⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ 'the Mind' (with apparent dittography or assimilation of ⲡ→ⲧ before ⲛ). The Light-Mind (νοῦς) is the technical Manichaean term for the descending intellectual savior. Confirmed by ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲥ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲁⲓ̈ⲛⲉ in line 32.
The repetition 'type, type' = 'type by type' — the descending Mind manifests in successive correspondential figures, each replicating the same divine pattern. Standard Manichaean typological idiom.
Lycopolitan = ϣⲁϫⲉ 'word, saying.' 'The five words' likely refers to the fivefold ritual formula (peace, right hand, kiss, etc.) by which the Mind greets the Church.
'Greet, embrace' — semantic match with ⲡⲁⲥⲡⲁⲥⲙⲟⲥ ('kiss/embrace') in line 33. The Mind's 'greeting' is the cosmological prototype of the ecclesial kiss of peace.
Restored as form of ⲧⲱⲍ 'join, mix, attach' (Sahidic ⲧⲱϩ) + 3sg.m suffix + ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ 'into the Church.' The Mind's drawing-and-joining concludes the soteriological reception sequence.

Restored as ἀσπασμὸς τῆς ἀγάπης 'kiss of love (agape)' — the holy kiss attested in Pauline letters (Rom 16:16, etc.) and continued as Manichaean ecclesial practice. The line-34 surviving ⲡⲏ confirms the ⲁⲅⲁⲡⲏ ending.
